claims.claim: The deficiency in mBols does not affect 55Fe incorporation into the [2Fe-2S] protein Grx5 from Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
claims.source: The deficiency in mBols did not elicit any significant decrease in 55Fe binding to these [2Fe-2S] proteins (Figure 2E,F).
claims.evidence: Supported by 55Fe radiolabeling data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Bol1-Bol3 are dedicated ISC assembly factors specifically involved in the maturation of a subset of mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] but not [2Fe-2S] proteins.
claims.source: We conclude that Bol1-Bol3 are dedicated ISC assembly factors specifically involved in the maturation of a subset of mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] but not of [2Fe-2S] proteins.
claims.evidence: Supported by 55Fe radiolabeling data showing defects in [4Fe-4S] proteins but not [2Fe-2S] proteins (Figure 2).

claims.claim: The mBols act after Grx5 in the ISC assembly pathway.
claims.source: Further, the mBols act after Grx5, the final core ISC component (Uzarska et al., 2013), because they were not needed for 55Fe incorporation into Grx5.
claims.evidence: Supported by 55Fe radiolabeling data showing normal Fe/S cluster incorporation into Grx5 in mBol-deficient cells (Figure 2F).

claims.claim: bol2Δ cells display a substantial activation of the Aft1-dependent FIT3 and FET3 genes.
claims.source: As expected (Kumanovics et al., 2008), bol2Δ cells displayed a substantial activation of the Aft1-dependent FIT3 and FET3 genes in a GFP-based promoter assay (Figure 3A–B).
claims.evidence: Supported by promoter activity assays shown in Figure 3A-B.

claims.claim: Yeast strains lacking BOL1 and/or BOL3 do not activate the iron regulon.
claims.source: In contrast, yeast strains lacking BOL1 and/or BOL3 behaved like wild-type cells indicating that the mBols are not involved in cellular iron regulation.
claims.evidence: Supported by promoter activity assays shown in Figure 3A-B showing no activation of FIT3 and FET3 in bol1Δ and bol3Δ cells.

claims.claim: nfu1Δ cells do not activate the iron regulon.
claims.source: This fits nicely to our conclusion above that Bol1-Bol3 do not belong to the core ISC system. The same situation was observed for cells lacking Nfu1 (Figure 3B), another known late-acting specific ISC assembly factor (Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by promoter activity assays shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Combining BOL2 deletion with BOL1 and/or BOL3 deletion activates the iron regulon more strongly than BOL2 deletion alone.
claims.source: Surprisingly, when the BOL2 deletion was combined with genetic ablation of BOL1 and/or BOL3, the iron regulon was activated slightly stronger than in bol2Δ cells (Figure 3A–B).
claims.evidence: Supported by promoter activity assays shown in Figure 3A-B.

claims.claim: Single BOL2 deletion does not cause major defects in cytosolic Fe/S protein maturation.
claims.source: Single BOL2 deletion is not associated with major phenotypes apart from iron homeostasis (Kumanovics et al., 2008) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: Supported by Leu1 activity measurements (Figure 3C) and 55Fe incorporation data (Figure 3D) showing minimal effects of BOL2 deletion alone.

claims.claim: Deletion of BOL1-BOL3 genes does not affect Leu1 enzyme activity.
claims.source: Second, we investigated the effects of the three BOL gene deletions on cytosolic Fe/S proteins by assaying the enzyme activity of isopropylmalate isomerase (Leu1). No changes were observed when BOL1-BOL3 genes were deleted either alone or in combination (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: bol2Δ cells show a twofold decrease in Leu1 activity.
claims.source: In contrast, bol2Δ cells showed a twofold decrease in Leu1 activity, which further declined upon additional deletion of BOL1-BOL3.
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Deletion of either BOL1-BOL3 or BOL2 alone hardly affects 55Fe/S cluster binding to Leu1.
claims.source: Deletion of either BOL1-BOL3 or BOL2 hardly affected 55Fe/S cluster binding to Leu1 indicating that neither mitochondrial Bol1-Bol3 nor cytosolic Bol2 perform a decisive role in Leu1 Fe/S cluster incorporation (Figure 3D,F).
claims.evidence: Supported by 55Fe radiolabeling data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Combining BOL2 deletion with BOL1 and/or BOL3 deletion results in up to twofold decrease in 55Fe/S cluster association with Leu1.
claims.source: However, combining the BOL2 deletion with that of BOL1 and/or BOL3 resulted in an up to twofold decrease in 55Fe/S cluster association with Leu1.
claims.evidence: Supported by 55Fe radiolabeling data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Triple BOL deletion (bol123Δ) results in a twofold decrease in 55Fe incorporation into the cytosolic Fe/S protein Rli1.
claims.source: A similar twofold decrease (compared to wild-type) was seen for 55Fe incorporation into another cytosolic Fe/S protein, the ABC protein Rli1 using the triple BOL deletion strain bol123Δ (Figure 3E–F).
claims.evidence: Supported by 55Fe radiolabeling data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: Any of the BOL genes can restore Rli1 maturation defect when reintroduced into bol123Δ mutant.
claims.source: The Rli1 maturation defect was completely restored when any of the BOL genes was reintroduced into the bol123Δ mutant.
claims.evidence: Supported by complementation experiments shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: nfu1Δ cells show diminished activities of both aconitase and SDH relative to wild type.
claims.source: As observed previously (Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011; Schilke et al., 1999), nfu1Δ cells showed a diminution in the activities of both aconitase and SDH relative to wild type (Figure 4A–B).
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Figure 4A-B.

claims.claim: Additional deletion of BOL3 in nfu1Δ cells causes a substantial further decrease in aconitase and SDH activities.
claims.source: A substantial further decrease to rather low aconitase and SDH activities was found for additional deletion of BOL3, but not of BOL1.
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Figure 4A-B.

claims.claim: Additional deletion of BOL1 in nfu1Δ cells does not cause further decrease in aconitase and SDH activities.
claims.source: A substantial further decrease to rather low aconitase and SDH activities was found for additional deletion of BOL3, but not of BOL1.
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Figure 4A-B.

claims.claim: Bol3 plays a distinct, Nfu1-independent role that cannot be executed by Bol1.
claims.source: These findings show that Bol3 plays a distinct, Nfu1-independent role that cannot be executed by Bol1.
claims.evidence: Supported by genetic interaction data showing that BOL3 but not BOL1 deletion exacerbates nfu1Δ defects (Figure 4A-B).

claims.claim: Bol3 cannot rescue any of the enzyme defects of nfu1Δ cells.
claims.source: In agreement with the growth behavior, Bol3 was not able to rescue any of the enzyme defects of nfu1Δ cells, while Nfu1 did so (Figure 4C–F, left).
claims.evidence: Supported by complementation experiments shown in Figure 4C-F.

claims.claim: Nfu1 cannot restore the enzyme activities of bol13Δ cells.
claims.source: Likewise, Nfu1 failed to restore the enzyme activities of bol13Δ cells, while Bol3 was complementing (Figure 4C–F, right).
claims.evidence: Supported by complementation experiments shown in Figure 4C-F.

claims.claim: Nfu1 and Bol3 cannot mutually substitute each other's biochemical function, even upon overproduction.
claims.source: These findings show that Nfu1 and Bol3 cannot mutually substitute each other's biochemical function, even upon overproduction.
claims.evidence: Supported by complementation experiments shown in Figure 4C-F and growth assays in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Human BOLA1 and BOLA3 have similar overall structural folds.
claims.source: According to the DALI server (Holm and Sander, 1993), both BOLA1 and BOLA3 show the highest structural similarity to BolA-like proteins from Arabidopsis thaliana, Babesia bovis, and Mus musculus (Abendroth et al., 2011; Kasai et al., 2004; Roret et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by NMR structural determination and comparison using DALI server.

claims.claim: The structural features of the loop between β1 and β2 differentiate BOLA1 from BOLA3.
claims.source: Apparently, the structural features of the loop between β1 and β2 are key for differentiating BOLA1 from BOLA3.
claims.evidence: Supported by NMR structural data showing different loop lengths and conformations between BOLA1 and BOLA3 (Figure 5).

claims.claim: His102 in BOLA1 and His96 in BOLA3 are invariant residues that may coordinate Fe/S clusters.
claims.source: Remarkably, this loop is closer to the 'invariant' His residue (His102 in BOLA1 and His96 in BOLA3; Figure 5), which has been shown to coordinate the [2Fe-2S] cluster in the yeast Bol2-Grx3 complex (Li et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by NMR structural data (Figure 5) and citation to previous work on Bol2-Grx3.

claims.claim: Apo-GLRX5 interacts with BOLA1 and BOLA3 with Kd values of 3 µM.
claims.source: This data fits nicely to thermophoresis results showing that both human BOLA proteins interacted with apo-GLRX5 with Kd values of 3 µM (Melber et al., 2016; accompanying manuscript).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to accompanying manuscript and NMR titration data showing 1:1 complex formation.

claims.claim: The interaction surface on GLRX5 in apo-GLRX5-BOLA complexes comprises the GSH binding site and its surroundings.
claims.source: The interaction surface on GLRX5 in the two complexes comprises the GSH binding site and its surroundings (Figure 6A,B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: Supported by NMR chemical shift perturbation analysis shown in Figure 6A-B.

claims.claim: The interaction surface on BOLAs with GLRX5 involves helix α2, part of the β-sheet and the invariant His residue.
claims.source: On the BOLAs, the interactions involve helix α2, part of the β-sheet and the invariant His residue (see above).
claims.evidence: Supported by NMR chemical shift perturbation analysis shown in Figure 6A-B.

claims.claim: BOLA1 stabilizes the [2Fe-2S] cluster of GLRX5 against reduction by dithionite.
claims.source: The cluster coordinated by the GLRX5-BOLA1 hetero-dimer was stable against reduction by dithionite creating a CD spectrum in which the peak at 460 nm was maintained but that at 400 nm was lost. In contrast, the cluster of holo-GLRX5 was destroyed upon dithionite treatment with no residual CD peaks (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Supported by CD spectroscopy data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: The [2Fe-2S] cluster of holo-GLRX5 is destroyed upon dithionite treatment.
claims.source: In contrast, the cluster of holo-GLRX5 was destroyed upon dithionite treatment with no residual CD peaks (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Supported by CD spectroscopy data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: BOLA3 does not stabilize the [2Fe-2S] cluster of GLRX5 against destruction by dithionite.
claims.source: Further, the Fe/S cluster was not protected against destruction by dithionite treatment indicating rather different coordination situations for the [2Fe-2S] clusters in the two GLRX5-BOLA heterodimers.
claims.evidence: Supported by CD spectroscopy data shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Gel filtration shows stable heterodimer formation between holo-GLRX5 and BOLA1.
claims.source: Holo-GLRX5 (recorded at 420 nm) eluted at 44 kDa indicative of homodimer with bound Fe/S cluster (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A). A significantly smaller molecular mass was observed for the heterodimeric GLRX5-BOLA1 (32 kDa), while the mixture of holo-GLRX5 and BOLA3 did not alter the elution behavior of GLRX5 at 420 nm.
claims.evidence: Supported by gel filtration data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Gel filtration does not show stable heterodimer formation between holo-GLRX5 and BOLA3.
claims.source: A significantly smaller molecular mass was observed for the heterodimeric GLRX5-BOLA1 (32 kDa), while the mixture of holo-GLRX5 and BOLA3 did not alter the elution behavior of GLRX5 at 420 nm.
claims.evidence: Supported by gel filtration data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: BOLA3 interacts with holo-NFU1 with higher affinity (Kd = 0.8 µM) than with apo-NFU1 (Kd = 3 µM).
claims.source: The dissociation constants (Kd) of the interactions were in the range of 3 µM, with the notable exception of a fourfold higher affinity detected for BOLA3 and holo-NFU1 (Kd = 0.8 µM).
claims.evidence: Supported by microscale thermophoresis data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: BOLA1 and BOLA3 interact with both apo-NFU1 and holo-NFU1 with Kd values around 3 µM.
claims.source: MST indeed showed a specific interaction between the two BOLA proteins and both apo- and holo-NFU1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 3). The dissociation constants (Kd) of the interactions were in the range of 3 µM, with the notable exception of a fourfold higher affinity detected for BOLA3 and holo-NFU1 (Kd = 0.8 µM).
claims.evidence: Supported by microscale thermophoresis data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Holo-GLRX5 preferentially cooperates with BOLA1.
claims.source: Collectively, these results data suggest that holo-GLRX5 preferentially cooperates with BOLA1, and holo-NFU1 with BOLA3.
claims.evidence: Supported by CD spectroscopy showing stable cluster coordination in GLRX5-BOLA1 complex and gel filtration showing stable heterodimer formation.

claims.claim: Holo-NFU1 preferentially cooperates with BOLA3.
claims.source: Collectively, these results data suggest that holo-GLRX5 preferentially cooperates with BOLA1, and holo-NFU1 with BOLA3.
claims.evidence: Supported by MST data showing higher affinity of BOLA3 for holo-NFU1 (Kd = 0.8 µM) compared to other interactions.

claims.claim: Lipoic acid synthase (LIAS) is the primary client of mBol function.
claims.source: Lipoic acid synthase (LIAS) with its two [4Fe-4S] clusters is the primary client of mBol function because of strong effects on lipoic acid-dependent proteins (such as PDH and KGDH) in bol13Δ cells.
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity data showing strong decreases in PDH and KGDH activities and lipoylation defects in bol13Δ cells (Figure 1).

claims.claim: The mBols act late in the ISC pathway, after the core ISC machinery and Grx5.
claims.source: Several findings allowed us to define the site of action of the mBols in the multi-step ISC assembly pathway (Figure 8). First, the mBols were not required for maturation of mitochondrial [2Fe-2S] proteins or cytosolic Fe/S proteins. Second, their deletion did not affect the yeast cellular iron regulon. These criteria distinguish the mBol phenotype from that of the components of the core ISC machinery including Grx5, that is the final core ISC factor (Uzarska et al., 2013), and suggest that mBols act subsequently to Grx5.
claims.evidence: Supported by multiple lines of evidence including lack of effects on [2Fe-2S] proteins, no iron regulon activation, and normal 55Fe incorporation into Grx5.

claims.claim: The mBols function after the Isa-Iba57 proteins in [4Fe-4S] cluster formation.
claims.source: Finally, the function of the mBols must be after the involvement of Isa-Iba57 proteins in the [4Fe-4S] cluster formation, because the mBols exhibit high [4Fe-4S] target specificity. In Isa-Iba57-defective cells, all mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] proteins and the non-Fe/S protein cytochrome oxidase are severely affected, unlike in bol13Δ cells (Mühlenhoff et al., 2011; Sheftel et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by comparison of phenotypes showing that bol13Δ cells have specific defects in a subset of [4Fe-4S] proteins, unlike the broad defects in Isa-Iba57 mutants.

claims.claim: Yeast is a suitable model system for the physiological and mechanistic investigation of mBols.
claims.source: This phenotypical resemblance suggests that the yeast mBols and at least human BOLA3 are functionally similar. Even though yeast appears to be a suitable model system for the physiological and mechanistic investigation of mBols, the two human BOLAs now need to be studied in cell culture to gain better insights into their relative function.
claims.evidence: Supported by the similarity between yeast bol13Δ phenotypes and human BOLA3 patient phenotypes.

claims.claim: Mitochondrial Fe/S protein biogenesis in yeast involves 17 known ISC components inherited from bacteria and conserved in eukaryotes.
claims.source: Mitochondrial Fe/S protein biogenesis in yeast involves 17 known ISC components which were inherited from bacteria and are conserved in eukaryotes (Johnson et al., 2005; Lill, 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published reviews.

claims.claim: The Isa1, Isa2 and Iba57 proteins cooperate to generate a [4Fe-4S] cluster.
claims.source: Even though the molecular mechanisms of this late phase of Fe/S protein biogenesis are poorly resolved, recent studies have shown that the Isa1, Isa2 and Iba57 proteins cooperate to generate a [4Fe-4S] cluster (Brancaccio et al., 2014; Gelling et al., 2008; Mühlenhoff et al., 2011; Sheftel et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published studies.

claims.claim: Nfu1 and Ind1 facilitate [4Fe-4S] cluster insertion into specific target apoproteins by transiently binding [4Fe-4S] clusters.
claims.source: Its insertion into specific target apoproteins is subsequently facilitated by Nfu1 and the P-loop ATPase Ind1, both transiently binding [4Fe-4S] clusters (Bych et al., 2008; Sheftel et al., 2009; Tong et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published studies.

claims.claim: Ind1 is specific for maturation of respiratory complex I.
claims.source: The latter ISC protein is specific for maturation of respiratory complex I, but nothing is known about the molecular mechanisms underlying [4Fe-4S] cluster insertion by eukaryotic Nfu1 and Ind1.
claims.evidence: Supported by established knowledge from cited studies.

claims.claim: Impairment of ISC factors involved in the second phase of Fe/S protein biogenesis only compromises mitochondrial function of yeast cells.
claims.source: While most proteins of the core ISC machinery are essential for cell viability, impairment of the ISC factors involved in the second phase of Fe/S protein biogenesis only compromises mitochondrial function of yeast cells.
claims.evidence: Supported by established knowledge and growth data showing that bol13Δ cells are viable but have respiratory defects.

claims.claim: The core ISC machinery plays a central role in cytosolic Fe/S protein biogenesis and cellular iron regulation.
claims.source: This striking difference for phases I and II is explained by the central, additional role of the core ISC machinery in both cytosolic Fe/S protein biogenesis and cellular iron regulation.
claims.evidence: Supported by established knowledge from cited reviews.

claims.claim: Functional defects of core ISC factors lead to impaired assembly of essential Fe/S proteins such as nuclear DNA polymerases and helicases.
claims.source: Functional defects of core ISC factors lead to impaired assembly of essential Fe/S proteins such as nuclear DNA polymerases and helicases (Gari et al., 2012; Netz et al., 2012; Stehling et al., 2012) and an induction of the yeast iron regulon involving the above mentioned Bol2 (Lill et al., 2012; Outten and Albetel, 2013; Paul and Lill, 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published studies.

claims.claim: Human BOLA3 belongs to a large protein family of bacterial origin.
claims.source: Human BOLA3 belongs to a large protein family of bacterial origin (Aldea et al., 1988; Willems et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published studies.

claims.claim: Eukaryotes such as yeast and humans possess three BOLA family members that can be discriminated by conserved sequence elements.
claims.source: Eukaryotes such as yeast and humans possess three BOLA family members that can be discriminated by conserved sequence elements (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Yeast Bol2 is cytosolic and involved in cellular iron regulation by forming heterodimeric [2Fe-2S] cluster-containing complexes with cytosolic monothiol glutaredoxins Grx3-Grx4.
claims.source: Yeast Bol2 (formerly termed Fra2; [Kumanovics et al., 2008]) is cytosolic, and is involved in cellular iron regulation by forming heterodimeric, [2Fe-2S] cluster-containing complexes with the cytosolic monothiol glutaredoxins Grx3-Grx4 (Li et al., 2009; Mühlenhoff et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published studies.

claims.claim: Human BOLA2 forms hetero-complexes with human GRX3.
claims.source: The human relative BOLA2 also forms hetero-complexes with human GRX3 (Banci et al., 2015; Li et al., 2012), yet the exact physiological role of the Bol2 proteins is still poorly defined.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to published studies.

claims.claim: Ablation of BOLA1 in cultured human cells increases mitochondrial protein thiol oxidation and elicits alterations in mitochondrial morphology.
claims.source: Ablation of BOLA1 in cultured human cells increases mitochondrial protein thiol oxidation and elicits alterations in mitochondrial morphology.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published study (Willems et al., 2013).

claims.claim: BOLA1 (but not BOLA3) co-purified with tagged mitochondrial monothiol glutaredoxin GLRX5.
claims.source: BOLA1 (but not BOLA3) co-purified with tagged mitochondrial monothiol glutaredoxin GLRX5 that is crucial for Fe/S protein biogenesis (Willems et al., 2013; Ye et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to published study.

claims.claim: PDH and KGDH activities are much more severely diminished in bol13Δ, bol123Δ, and nfu1Δ cells grown in lactate medium compared to galactose medium.
claims.source: In contrast, PDH and KGDH activities were much more severely (ten- vs. threefold) diminished in bol13Δ, bol123Δ, and nfu1Δ cells grown in lactate medium, similar to previous reports on Isa protein depletion (Kaut et al., 2000; Mühlenhoff et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity measurements comparing growth in lactate vs. galactose media (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5).

claims.claim: The overall topology of the solution structure of human BOLA3 is α1β1β2η1α2η2β3.
claims.source: The overall topology of the solution structure of human BOLA3 is α1β1β2η1α2η2β3 (h: 310-helix), in which β1 and β2 are antiparallel, and β3 is parallel to β2 (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by NMR structural determination shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: The overall topology of the solution structure of BOLA1 is α1η1β1β2η2α2α3β3α4.
claims.source: The overall topology of the solution structure of BOLA1 is similar to that of BOLA3, with the exception of the presence, in BOLA1, of short helices in the loop regions and at the C-terminus (α1η1β1β2η2α2α3β3α4 topology) (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by NMR structural determination shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: BOLA1 has approximately 15 unstructured residues at both N and C termini.
claims.source: In addition, at both termini BOLA1 has ca. 15 residues that are unstructured and whose backbone NH resonances are clustered in the central region of the 1H-15N HSQC spectrum (part B).
claims.evidence: Supported by NMR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The N and C termini of BOLA1 are highly flexible.
claims.source: The 15N backbone relaxation properties showed that the N and C termini of BOLA1 are highly flexible, as about 15 to 20 residues on each terminus have negative 15N NOE values, while the folded domain is essentially rigid.
claims.evidence: Supported by 15N relaxation NMR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: BOLA3 is a rigid molecule with the exception of terminal residues and residues around the invariant His96.
claims.source: BOLA3 is a rigid molecule, with the exception of the first detected residue at the N terminus, the last two residues at the C terminus and residues around invariant His96. All of them experience fast backbone motions in the ns-ps time scale, as indicated by their low or negative 15N NOE values.
claims.evidence: Supported by 15N relaxation NMR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: There is a high degree of organismic variability in the precise interaction mode between Grx and Bol proteins.
claims.source: We conclude that there is a high degree of organismic variability in the precise interaction mode between Grx and Bol proteins.
claims.evidence: Supported by comparison of NMR chemical shift data between human and Arabidopsis thaliana complexes showing different interaction regions (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).

claims.claim: The CD spectrum of GLRX5-BOLA1 differs from holo-GLRX5 with a positive versus negative ellipticity around 400 nm and changes at 460 nm.
claims.source: The CD spectrum of GLRX5-BOLA1 characteristically differed from that of holo-GLRX5 in a positive versus negative ellipticity around 400 nm with a 6 nm blue shift and 40% decrease of the ~460 nm peak with a 6 nm red shift (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: Supported by CD spectroscopy data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: The spectral changes in GLRX5-BOLA1 complex saturate at an equimolar ratio suggesting high affinity equimolar hetero-complex formation.
claims.source: These spectral changes saturated at an equimolar ratio of holo-GLRX5 and BOLA1 suggesting a high affinity equimolar hetero-complex formation with a shared [2Fe-2S] cluster (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by CD titration data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The CD signal decrease in GLRX5-BOLA3 complex mainly depends on the presence of GSH.
claims.source: We found a general decrease of the CD peaks upon GLRX5-BOLA3 hetero-complex formation (Figure 7C). These changes mainly depended on the presence of GSH, and not salt or pH (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: Supported by CD spectroscopy data comparing different buffer conditions shown in Figure 7C-D.

claims.claim: The CD signal decrease in GLRX5-BOLA3 complex does not reach saturation even after addition of more than tenfold molar excess of BOLA3.
claims.source: In all cases, the CD signal decrease did not reach saturation even after addition of a more than tenfold molar excess of BOLA3 over holo-GLRX5. This result indicated a rather low affinity for this interference of BOLA3 with the [2Fe-2S] cluster.
claims.evidence: Supported by CD titration data shown in Figure 7C-D.

claims.claim: Double deletion of BOL3 and NFU1 exacerbates the defects of SDH and LIAS compared to single deletions.
claims.source: A specific genetic interaction of NFU1 and BOL3 supports our biochemical findings. Double deletion of these genes exacerbated the defects of SDH and LIAS, whereas simultaneous deletions of NFU1 and BOL1 did not (Figure 4A and B).
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Figure 4A-B.

claims.claim: Simultaneous deletions of NFU1 and BOL1 do not exacerbate defects compared to nfu1Δ alone.
claims.source: Double deletion of these genes exacerbated the defects of SDH and LIAS, whereas simultaneous deletions of NFU1 and BOL1 did not (Figure 4A and B).
claims.evidence: Supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Figure 4A-B.

results.result: Yeast Bol1 and Bol3 are localized exclusively in the mitochondrial matrix, as demonstrated by cell fractionation and protease protection assays.
results.evaluation: Claim C12 is supported by cell fractionation experiments showing exclusive mitochondrial localization and sub-fractionation studies demonstrating matrix localization similar to known matrix proteins Tim44 and Mge1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).

results.result: Bol1 and Bol3 function as specific mitochondrial ISC assembly factors that facilitate [4Fe-4S] cluster insertion into a subset of mitochondrial proteins, particularly lipoate synthase (LIAS) and succinate dehydrogenase (SDH), with largely overlapping but not identical functions.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C4, C30, and C65 are well-supported by multiple lines of evidence including enzyme activity assays showing decreased PDH, KGDH, and SDH activities in bol13Δ cells (Figure 1), 55Fe radiolabeling showing reduced cluster incorporation into [4Fe-4S] but not [2Fe-2S] proteins (Figure 2), lipoylation defects (Figure 1F), and complementation experiments (Figures 1—figure supplement 4, 2D). The data consistently demonstrate that only double deletion creates significant defects, supporting functional overlap.

results.result: Single deletions of BOL1 or BOL3 have minimal effects on Fe/S enzyme activities, while double BOL1-BOL3 deletions result in substantial decreases in Fe/S cluster-dependent enzyme activities (except aconitase), creating a weak respiratory defect.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C18 are supported by growth assays on non-fermentable carbon sources (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and comprehensive enzyme activity measurements (Figure 1A-E). The data show that single deletions have minimal effects except for a slight SDH decrease in bol3Δ, while double deletions cause substantial (up to threefold) decreases in SDH, PDH, and KGDH activities, with aconitase notably unaffected. Additional BOL2 deletion does not exacerbate effects.

results.result: The decreased SDH activity in bol13Δ cells is due to direct defects in Fe/S cluster assembly rather than protein level changes, and both BOL1 and BOL3 can rescue these deficiencies when reintroduced.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C21 are supported by immunoblot data showing unchanged SDH protein levels despite decreased activity (Figure 1F), lipoylation defects of PDH and KGDH E2 subunits (Figure 1F), and complementation experiments demonstrating rescue of SDH activity by reintroduction of BOL1 or BOL3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).

results.result: 55Fe radiolabeling experiments demonstrate that mBol deficiency specifically affects [4Fe-4S] protein maturation (SDH, HiPIP) but not [2Fe-2S] proteins (aconitase, FDX2, Grx5), with BOL3 deletion showing stronger effects than BOL1 deletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C29 are supported by comprehensive 55Fe incorporation assays (Figure 2A-F) showing no significant effects on aconitase or [2Fe-2S] proteins (FDX2, SpGrx5), but 40% decrease in SDH and 60% decrease in HiPIP upon BOL3 deletion. Single BOL1 deletion has no effects. Complementation with Bol1 or Bol3 restores activity, while Bol2 or Grx5 do not (Figure 2D), demonstrating specificity.

results.result: The mBols act late in the ISC assembly pathway, after the core ISC machinery including Grx5, and after the Isa-Iba57 proteins involved in [4Fe-4S] cluster formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C31, C66, and C67 are supported by multiple lines of evidence: normal 55Fe incorporation into Grx5 in mBol-deficient cells (Figure 2F), lack of effects on [2Fe-2S] proteins, no iron regulon activation (Figure 3A-B), and phenotypic comparison showing specific defects in a subset of [4Fe-4S] proteins unlike the broad defects in Isa-Iba57 mutants. The logical inference from these observations is sound.

results.result: Deletion of BOL1 and/or BOL3 does not activate the iron regulon, unlike BOL2 deletion, but combining BOL2 deletion with BOL1/BOL3 deletion activates the iron regulon more strongly than BOL2 deletion alone.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C35 are supported by promoter activity assays (Figure 3A-B) showing substantial FIT3 and FET3 activation in bol2Δ cells but not in bol1Δ, bol3Δ, or nfu1Δ cells. Combined deletions (bol2Δ with bol1Δ/bol3Δ) show slightly stronger activation than bol2Δ alone, with specificity confirmed by complementation experiments.

results.result: Neither mitochondrial Bol1-Bol3 nor cytosolic Bol2 are directly required for cytosolic Fe/S protein maturation, but combined deletion of all three BOL genes results in modest defects in cytosolic Fe/S proteins (Leu1, Rli1).
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C42 are supported by Leu1 enzyme activity measurements (Figure 3C) and 55Fe incorporation assays (Figure 3D-E) showing minimal effects of single deletions but up to twofold decreases in combined deletions. The effects are weak compared to known CIA deficiencies, supporting the interpretation that these are indirect effects. Complementation with any BOL gene restores Rli1 maturation (Figure 3E).

results.result: Bol1-Bol3 and Nfu1 perform distinct, non-overlapping functions in mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] protein maturation, with Bol3 playing a specific Nfu1-independent role that cannot be executed by Bol1, and neither protein can complement the other's function even upon overexpression.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C43-C49, C94-C95 are supported by genetic interaction studies showing that BOL3 but not BOL1 deletion exacerbates nfu1Δ defects (Figure 4A-B), complementation experiments demonstrating that Bol3 cannot rescue nfu1Δ defects and Nfu1 cannot rescue bol13Δ defects (Figure 4C-F), and growth assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). The data consistently demonstrate functional specificity and non-redundancy between these proteins.

results.result: Human BOLA1 and BOLA3 have similar overall structural folds but differ in key structural features, particularly the loop between β1 and β2, with both containing conserved His residues (His102 in BOLA1, His96 in BOLA3) near potential Fe/S cluster binding regions.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C52, C84-C88 are supported by NMR structural determination (Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 1) showing similar topologies but different loop structures and flexibility patterns. The structures show conserved His residues in positions consistent with potential Fe/S cluster coordination. DALI server comparisons confirm similarity to other BolA-like proteins. The 15N relaxation data support the flexibility assessments.

results.result: Apo-BOLA1 and apo-BOLA3 form 1:1 heterodimeric complexes with apo-GLRX5 with Kd values of 3 μM, involving the GSH binding site on GLRX5 and helix α2, part of the β-sheet, and the invariant His residue on BOLAs.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C53-C55 are supported by NMR titration experiments showing 1:1 complex formation (Figure 6A-B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1-2), NMR relaxation data indicating heterodimeric complexes (Figure 6—figure supplement 3), and chemical shift perturbation analysis mapping interaction surfaces. The Kd values are supported by citation to accompanying manuscript and consistent with NMR data showing saturation at 1:1 ratio.

results.result: BOLA1 stabilizes the [2Fe-2S] cluster of GLRX5 against dithionite reduction and forms a stable heterodimer, while BOLA3 does not stabilize the cluster and shows only weak, GSH-dependent interaction with holo-GLRX5, suggesting preferential cooperation of holo-GLRX5 with BOLA1.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C56-C60, C63, C90-C93 are supported by CD spectroscopy showing distinct spectral features and dithionite stability for GLRX5-BOLA1 but not GLRX5-BOLA3 (Figure 7A-D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), gel filtration showing stable heterodimer formation only with BOLA1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), and titration data showing saturation for BOLA1 but not BOLA3. The data consistently demonstrate differential cluster stabilization.

results.result: BOLA1 and BOLA3 interact with both apo-NFU1 and holo-NFU1 with Kd values around 3 μM, with BOLA3 showing fourfold higher affinity for holo-NFU1 (Kd = 0.8 μM), suggesting preferential cooperation of holo-NFU1 with BOLA3.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C61-C62, C64 are supported by microscale thermophoresis data (Figure 7—figure supplement 3) showing specific interactions with measured Kd values. The fourfold higher affinity of BOLA3 for holo-NFU1 compared to other interactions is clearly demonstrated. Control experiments with non-interacting proteins (FDX2, cytochrome c, RNase A) support specificity.

results.result: Yeast is a suitable model system for investigating mBol function based on phenotypic similarity between yeast bol13Δ cells and human BOLA3 patient cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C68 is supported by the demonstrated similarity in phenotypes: both yeast bol13Δ cells and human BOLA3 patients show major defects in lipoic acid-dependent enzymes and respiratory complexes I and II (claims C9-C11, supported by citations). The inference that yeast is a suitable model is reasonable given this phenotypic conservation, though the authors appropriately note that human BOLAs need further study in cell culture.

results.result: PDH and KGDH activities are much more severely diminished (tenfold vs. threefold) in bol13Δ, bol123Δ, and nfu1Δ cells grown in lactate medium compared to galactose medium.
results.evaluation: Claim C83 is supported by enzyme activity measurements comparing growth in different media (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5), showing that respiratory conditions exacerbate defects in lipoic acid-dependent enzymes but not in aconitase or SDH. This is consistent with previous reports on Isa protein depletion.

results.result: There is high organismic variability in the precise interaction mode between Grx and Bol proteins, as demonstrated by differences between human and Arabidopsis thaliana complexes.
results.evaluation: Claim C89 is supported by comparison of NMR chemical shift data between human GLRX5-BOLA complexes and A. thaliana GrxS14-BolA2 complexes (Figure 6—figure supplement 4), showing different interaction regions. The human complexes show involvement of the invariant His region and specific GLRX5 helices that differ from the plant complexes.

results.result: Background information on BOLA3 disease associations, ISC pathway components, and previous characterization of BOLA family proteins from the literature.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C11, C69, C71-C82 are background claims supported by citations to published literature. These establish the context for the study, including the association of BOLA3 mutations with MMDS2, the known components of the ISC pathway, and previous characterization of BOLA family proteins. The citations appear appropriate and the claims are consistent with established knowledge.
